topic.title: Long-Video Reasoning and Evidence Selection
topic.overview: This topic focuses on reasoning over extended video rather than simply encoding its content. Methods select frames, divide activities into subtasks, use external tools, or maintain temporal context to answer questions and assess progress. A central design choice is how much evidence to examine at each reasoning step.
topic.whyItMatters: Processing every frame equally can be expensive and distract from decisive events. Conversely, aggressive selection can omit the moment that changes the answer, especially when an action fails or departs from the expected sequence.
topic.evolution: Early representatives connect contextual clips and learn video-script knowledge in 2021. Later frameworks introduce recursive decomposition, frame-based reasoning chains, and long-video benchmarks. A 2026 reasoning suite adds large-scale tasks and verifiable scoring, reflecting an effort to distinguish reasoning quality from persuasive descriptions.
openQuestions: Can evidence-selection policies recognize when they have missed a critical event?
How should tests distinguish temporal reasoning from memorized event templates?

papers.tldr: VideoTrace-R1 improves long-video reasoning by symbolically checking and rewarding intermediate temporal claims against structured event traces.

papers.title: VideoVeritas: AI-Generated Video Detection via Perception Pretext Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: VideoVeritas improves AI-generated video detection by training fine-grained perception through grounding and counting tasks alongside fact-based reasoning.

papers.title: WatchLog: Efficient and Interpretable Event Reasoning for Endpoint Detection and Response Logs with Multimodal LLMs
papers.tldr: WatchLog represents endpoint logs as video sequences to improve threat detection, temporal reasoning, and behavior explanations.
